# ADR-1086: Prime project memories from explicit shell file cues

## Evidence

The native Codex reproduction on 2026-09-22 sent `Bash` PostToolUse for
`cat read-me.txt`, with `tool_input.command`, an absolute `cwd`, and plain
stdout in `tool_response`. A failed `cat missing-file.txt` sent the same
hook with error text and no exit code. A yielded `sleep 2; cat read-me.txt`
sent one Bash PostToolUse after completion, and no separate write_stdin
hook. These were captured with Codex 0.154.0; fixture-shaped tests preserve
this contract in `tests_py/hooks/test_shell_read_events.py`. The original
three explicit-file native reproduction cases failed before this change.

The existing hook recognized Read/Edit/Write only, used a direct PostgreSQL
connection regardless of the selected backend, and updated historical and
unrelated-project rows. ADR-0496 defines the existing 0.1 increment and
60-second cooldown; this decision changes cue delivery and scope, not their
values or retrieval scoring.

## Decision

Parse explicit file operands of simple `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed` print,
and `rg` commands with shlex. Resolve operands against the command working
directory and retain existing regular files. Resolve symlinks and deduplicate
paths. Do not execute text, expand wildcards, recursively guess files read
from directories, or interpret compound commands, redirections, variable
expansion, command substitutions, unknown options, or sed write/execute scripts.
An unrecognized command supplies no reliable explicit file cue.

A native plain-output Bash PostToolUse supplies a completed **attempted
access cue**. It does not prove successful reading: native Codex omits the
exit status. Never parse stdout, including JSON-looking stdout, as execution
metadata. Explicit structured exit-code failures do not activate memories.
For hosts supplying structured asynchronous process IDs, persist pending
paths under the hook state root, keyed by session plus process ID; consume
them only on matching successful completion. Interactive input invalidates
the pending cue. Never join another thread or an unmatched transcript event.

Choose the configured store through the shared backend factory. One atomic
UPDATE applies all file cues in a tool call, so a row matching several cues
receives one increment. Include only current, nonstale, nonbenchmark rows
below the heat cap that match the project root/ancestors or are global.
Unknown project means globals only (ADR-1080). Team visibility does not
bypass project scope (ADR-1083). Escape literal SQL LIKE metacharacters.
Use the common connection adapter, explicit commit/rollback, and preserve
last_accessed/heat_base_set_at refresh without incrementing access_count.
Do not close the process-shared store after an operation.

Cooldown keys contain the canonical project and file path, so relative paths
and symlink aliases cannot bypass a cooldown and different project contexts
do not suppress each other. The cache remains disposable as in ADR-0496.

## Verification

`test_preemptive_native.py` reproduces the three originally missed cues.
`test_shell_read_paths.py` covers exact operands and rejected syntax.
`test_shell_read_events.py` covers native plain stdout, missing files,
structured failure, asynchronous correlation, canonical paths, and batching.
`test_file_memory_priming.py` runs the same real-store scope, supersession,
staleness, benchmark, escaping, heat-cap and timestamp assertions against
SQLite and a newly created disposable PostgreSQL database. It also checks
rollback and shared connection ownership at the failure boundary.
Native execution is a separate release validation: fixtures alone do not
prove that Codex loaded or executed the published hook.

## Consequences

Both supported storage backends now receive scoped priming from explicit
shell file cues. Broader shell execution semantics remain the host's domain;
inferring reads from arbitrary programs or command stdout would fabricate
provenance. ASCII case-insensitive substring matching is portable; SQLite's
built-in LOWER does not promise PostgreSQL's Unicode case behavior.
